name: Parliament-Funkadelic
hook: George Clinton ran the same musicians as two bands under two names and two contracts, so no single label dispute could ever shut the music down.
blurb: George Clinton's doo-wop group, the Parliaments, got stuck in a contract dispute with their label, Revilot, in 1968, so Clinton started recording the same musicians under a new name, Funkadelic, to keep working. By 1970 he had the rights to the old name back too, and ran Parliament and Funkadelic side by side, on different labels, with the same band underneath: Parliament's horn-driven, vocal-group funk and Funkadelic's psychedelic, guitar-led version. The set-up produced the riffs, chants and basslines that made them hip-hop's second-biggest sample source after James Brown's band. Casablanca Records, under its founder Neil Bogart, signed Parliament in 1974 and spent heavily on their costumed live show, including a hundred-foot spaceship, the Mothership, that landed onstage, one of the most extravagant bets any label made on a Black funk act in the 1970s. Legal tangles over the many names forced Clinton to dissolve both bands in 1981.

signatureTracks.title: Get Off Your Ass and Jam

signatureTracks.title: One Nation Under a Groove
